name: Redwood Interior
desc: Deep inside an old-growth redwood grove looking through the trunks — four ranks of colossal columns recede into lit fog, each rank hazier and drifting at its own rate so the gaps between them open and close in parallax, volumetric shafts rake down between the boles with pollen turning in them, and a fern understory catches the last light along the duff; coastal old growth, a moonlit nocturne, autumn gold hour, sumi ink wash, or a cyan blueprint.

energy.doc: how hard the light works — shaft brightness, rim light on trunks, mote glow

scale.doc: how monumental the boles are — trunk width and height, spacing (rebuilds the grove)

density.doc: how many trunks per rank, ferns, dust motes and shafts

speed.doc: fog scroll, mote fall and fern sway rate

shafts.doc: strength and count of the volumetric light shafts

fog.doc: how thick the fog is — how far back the ranks fade

hue.doc: palette hue shift off the default red-brown bark

x.doc: which way the light rakes — which side of each trunk is lit and how the shafts lean

y.doc: the forest-floor line — low y raises the trunks and drops the understory

style.doc: aesthetic: oldgrowth = coastal red-brown boles in green-gold backlit fog; nocturne = cold moonlit blue-silver, near-monochrome; autumn = amber gold-hour shafts, warm duff; ink = sumi ink-wash tonal trunks, no colour; blueprint = cyan schematic, trunks as measured centrelines, no photo shading

act.doc: multi-minute programme — the grove calm, wind combing the crowns and loosening debris, or fog steadily thickening and rising over minutes

seed.doc: regenerates the trunk placement, bark, ferns and fog banks

alpha.doc: how far the world sits back behind the performers
